title: Zetrix AI says unable to repay RM2 bil sukuk now, expects 15% revenue hit from JPJ suspension
text:
Zetrix AI says unable to repay RM2 bil sukuk now, expects 15% revenue hit from JPJ suspension Saturday 14 Nov 2026 BURSA SGX Home 
 Highlight Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 13): Financially troubled Zetrix AI Bhd (KL: ZETRIX ) on Friday admitted that it is currently unable to repay the entire RM2 billion outstanding under its sukuk programme. The company also said that the suspension of its services as a collection agent for the Road Transport Department (JPJ) is expected to reduce its revenue by about 15%.
 In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Zetrix AI said it had proposed amendments to the covenants governing its sukuk wakalah programme, although discussions with sukukholders are still ongoing.
 The proposals include allowing managing director Wong Thean Soon and parties acting in concert with him to collectively remain the single largest shareholder, instead of requiring Wong to individually hold that position.
 It also proposed allowing the company to charge up to 10% of its net assets as security for financing facilities, with the proceeds to be placed in an escrow account to meet its sukuk repayment obligations.
 However, the company acknowledged that a further breach had arisen following its failure to repay RM25 million due under the sukuk programme.
 “The next meeting with the sukukholders has not been fixed pending the latest development in regards to a further breach where the repayment of an amount of RM25 million has not been made. The company intends to repay this amount before the meeting with the sukukholders was to be held,” it said.
 Separately, Zetrix AI said its proposal to settle outstanding remittances to JPJ remained under government evaluation.
 The proposal involves ring-fencing future collections and making several lump-sum payments over a short period to settle the outstanding amounts, which it said remained unchanged.
 The suspension of Zetrix AI and its subsidiary MyEG Sdn Bhd as JPJ collection agents is expected to reduce group revenue by approximately 15%, based on JPJ's contribution as at end-2025, with a direct impact on profitability.
 However, the company said while it could not yet determine the indirect impact over the next two quarters, it was reducing the number of physical e-service centres as part of efforts to “right-size its operations”.
 On its outstanding final dividend of 2.89 sen per share for the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025, Zetrix AI disclosed that 25 central depository system (CDS) accounts were affected, involving RM49.76 million.
 It said its board was obtaining an independent legal opinion on litigation involving the dividend reinvestment plan, and considered withholding the affected payments appropriate while determining its next course of action.
 Zetrix AI also defended its decision to withdraw the first interim dividend for 2026, saying that although the board had initially assessed the company as solvent following the dividend declaration, subsequent developments necessitated conserving working capital to meet its commitments.
 “The current events impacting the company has compelled the board to make a difficult and prudent decision to withdraw the 2026 interim dividend in order to conserve the company’s working capital to meet its commitment,” it said.
 Bursa Malaysia has directed Zetrix AI to settle all outstanding cash dividends no later than Nov 23.
 Meanwhile, the company said it would contest additional income tax assessments totalling RM353.13 million imposed by the Inland Revenue Board, arising from disputes over transfer pricing and deemed interest for the assessment years 2021 to 2023.
 It said the assessments had no immediate impact on operations or financials, although an unsuccessful legal challenge could result in an obligation to settle the additional taxes. Case management is scheduled for Nov 20.
 On corporate governance, Zetrix AI said it was working to appoint new independent directors and reconstitute its board committees before the deadline for releasing its third quarter results for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026.
 The company also expects to appoint a new external auditor by the end of November following the resignation of TGS TW PLT as announced on Sept 28. It said it had sought proposals from “three reputable firms and intends to finalise the appointment of the auditor before the commencement of the audit for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026”.
 Regarding its employee share option scheme, the company said the exercise was intended to reward and retain long-serving employees who had served for the past 26 years, while potentially raising RM42.6 million if all options are exercised.
 The exchange had given Zetrix AI until Friday to provide the requested information, while separately directing it to settle outstanding dividends owed to unaffected shareholders by Nov 23.
 Shares in Zetrix AI closed unchanged at six sen on Friday, after earlier falling to five sen, valuing the company at RM473.9 million. The stock has plunged 92.29% from its year-to-date high of 85.8 sen on April 21.
